findings.title: Activity verification assumes an obsolete request and fingerprint shape
evidence: VenuePanel.vue:74 sends normal command(activity, {id:card.id}); client.ts:643 places this in payload, with no top-level id. outgoing(activity,payload) retains payload.
protocol.ts:128-130 concatenates JSON([cityId,type,id,mode]) with canonical JSON payload. Missing top-level id and mode become null in the array.
core.ts:258-266 uses ordinary action authority, with no prefix. once.ts:170 bounds fingerprints longer than the existing limit.

Helper receiptType at line41 attempts JSON.parse on the complete concatenated fingerprint. Its verify-local-activity-result branch at line52 repeats the parse and compares array element2 to the observed activity ID. Neither matches the normal browser request.
types.ts:42 notes Worker receipts omit type, which makes receiptType reject such a fingerprint before the later ID check. A stored type alone would not fix the later parse/ID check.

derivedExample.scope: Derived from exact source; no actual stored receipt or browser completion claimed.

findings.fix: Same existing Cloud Astra owner should match exact canonical full or bounded fingerprint of normal UI activity payload {id:witness.id}, with city/type and the successful receipt ID tied to the observed natural action witness. Pin and reuse canonical server fingerprint/bounding logic or a narrowly reviewed exact equivalent. Do not change game request/receipt formats, submit actions outside the normal UI, or weaken the successful completion proof.

limits: Source analysis and isolated JSON parsing only; no reviewed executable run, browser, HTTP, SQLite, funding, stage or restart.
Earlier source supported arrival/activity defaults remain valid; this is a verification helper defect.
Controller bounds and all gameplay source remain unchanged. Runtime launch remains held until corrected immutable source is reviewed.
